A Neural Network
 • Imagine you are given many pictures of faces (48 Million pixels),
  and you’re asked to identify one of 1000 possible people.
 • Imagine you are given speech waves and you’re asked to to
   identify for each, which of 25 sounds each speech wave
   corresponds to.
 • What can do this? A Neural Network (NN)
 •  I will not tell you now why it’s called a NN. I will teach you what it is
   by what it does– how it walks and how it swims.
 • The job of an NN is to take a bunch of numbers the 48M pixels in
  one image/numbers of a wave and to return a probability
   distribution.
 • For speech the probability distribution is 25 sounds
 • But let’s say it had just 5 vowels, this is a pdf: [.2,.2,.4,.2,0]
 • And let’s say we agree the vowel order is read, rad, rude, Rud, rod
 • The p’s must sum to 1 (100%)
 • That says: there’s 20% chance the sound is the v in read, 20% it’s
   the vowel in rad, 40% the vowel in rude, 20% it’s the vowel in Rud,

A Neural Network
 • The input of an NN is a bunch of numbers, signal, or a vector, e.g., [4,1,-3,2,1,.4,1,2,-
   3,…] (usually 1000’s of nums). Let’s say these are the pressure numbers of a speech
  wave
 • The output of the NN is a decision pdf: Given the signal, what’s the p(each object): p of
  each vowels read, rad, rude, Rud, rod
 • How? How can NNs do that? How can it make a decision.
 • They have knowledge, in a bunch of weights w’s
 • And somehow the input signal vector is combined with these w’s and a decision
   about the object detected is made, eventually, as there are many many w’s and many
  many calculations! Several trillion w’s and billions of calculations.
 • These magical w’s allow the NN to make decisions, but how does it know these w’s???
 • Fake it till you make it!
 • SGD for NNs. You start out with random w’s.
       1.  Give it a signal (let’s say we give it the vowel in Rud)
       2.  Forward Propagation: It uses its stupid w’s, and it produces a pdf that doesn’t reflect reality:
            [.4,.1,.2,.2,.1]
       3. We tell it: NO!!!!!!! You should have decided: 0,0,0,1,0], so it realizes it made a big Error or Loss
       4.  It improves its w’s to reduce the Loss
       5.  Give it another signal and repeat billions of times!

Two Huge Questions

1. Learning: How does an NN learn the w’s? Specifically
2. Inference: How does an NN combine w’s with inputs?
   Specifically
• We will answer question 2 first, since 2 is part of 1!!!

Beliefs: Not on exam!

Most engineers/neuroscientists/people: Modern AI has nothing
to do with how humans think, perceive, act, decide, etc. The brain
is full of chemistry and electrical activity and abstract stuff, and
that obviously is not part of LLMs, which are full of numbers and
arithmetic!



A few people, including me: Modern AI is a set of evolutionary
tinkerings for 100 years with how arithmetic can emulate brain
chemical and electrical activity… And these attempts seem to
have succeeded.
